newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says talks with PLO on again in Cairo.
newsitem.headline: Israel says talks with PLO on again in Cairo.

text.p: Israel said it would go ahead with peace talks with the Palestinians in Cairo on Sunday after the PLO denied having an agreement for the Jewish state to stop building settlements.

"In Israel we heard the denial that the Palestinians put out that there was any sort of agreement with Israel on a halt of settlements. Following the Palestinian denial, the Israeli delegation is leaving now for the talks in Cairo," said Israeli spokesman Shai Bazak. Palestinian officials said the talks would begin at 1430 GMT.
PLO officials said earler that Israel had agreed in principle to an unspecified "pause" in Jewish settlement building.
As a result Israel said it would refuse to take part in revived peace talks with the Palestinians on Sunday until the PLO retracted the statements.
In Cairo, senior Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat cleared the way for the meeting by saying Israel had not agreed to any preconditions on settlement building.
Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu's 66-54 majority in parliament could crumble if he stopped Jewish settlement backed by religious and right-wing legislators in his government.
